sections.title: 1. Disclosed trade volume, Jan 1, 2025 – Sep 24, 2026 (by transaction date)
notes: Totals are the sums of the reported ranges: the minimum is the sum of range floors, the maximum is the sum of range ceilings.

*Ten House transactions used open-ended bands ("Spouse/DC Over $1,000,000" or "Over $50,000,000"). Their floor is counted and their ceiling is unknown, so the maximum is a lower bound. The all-assets figures include Treasury bills, money-market funds, municipal bonds, and one interest-rate-cap transaction. That is why the stock-and-option subset is also shown.

Coverage: 161 members with at least one electronically filed trade. Excluded (scanned paper filings that cannot be machine-read): 112 House PTRs from 17 members (e.g., Reps. Ro Khanna (20 filings), Hal Rogers (19), Michael McCaul (18), Tony Wied (13), Diana Harshbarger (11), Chuck Fleischmann (9)) and 30 Senate paper PTRs, all from Sen. Richard Blumenthal. The true totals are therefore higher than shown.

sections.title: 2. Top traders by disclosed volume (sum of range minimums, all assets)
notes: Stocks and options only, top 5: Pelosi $24.0M–$102.1M (31 transactions); Shreve $16.1M–$42.0M; Fields $11.7M–$31.1M; Gottheimer $10.5M–$41.9M; McCormick $9.9M–$31.7M.
Most transactions: Cisneros 1,588; Lisa McClain 1,375; Sen. Alan Armstrong 707; Rob Bresnahan 653; Shreve 634.
Many high-count filers use managed or advisor accounts. The filings often say so (e.g., "Filing Status" or "Description" notes). Volume by itself shows nothing about intent.
sections.label: Verified by SwampForce

sections.title: 3. Filings made more than 45 days after the trade (STOCK Act)
notes: Face-of-filing result: 2,795 transaction lines filed in 2025–2026 were reported more than 45 days after the transaction date shown on the filing. They come from 63 members.
Largest by number of late lines (each checked against the official filing):
Some late lines may be dating errors on the form. One Shreve line shows a 3,698-day lag, which is almost certainly a typo.
Some may cover transactions from before the person was a covered official (new members and appointees).
Some may be voluntary disclosures of assets that are not covered.
The House and Senate Ethics Committees assess and waive the $200 fee privately. There is no public list of fees paid.
sections.label: Verified by SwampForce

sections.title: 4. Members of Congress actually charged with or convicted of insider trading (primary records)
notes: No sitting member was charged with insider trading in 2025–2026, based on DOJ and SEC releases searched. No one has ever been criminally prosecuted solely for late STOCK Act disclosure. The statutory remedy is the ethics-committee late fee.

trading-28.title: Rule: A member must report a covered transaction "not later than 30 days after receiving notification" of it, "but in no case…
lines: Rule: A member must report a covered transaction "not later than 30 days after receiving notification" of it, "but in no case later than 45 days after such transaction." This is the STOCK Act, Pub. L. 112-105, §6 (congress.gov), codified at 5 U.S.C. 13105(l) (uscode.house.gov).
trading-28.label: Verified by SwampForce

trading-29.title: Rep. Christopher Collins (R-NY)
lines: Charge / court: S.D.N.Y. No. 18-cr-567. Conspiracy to commit securities fraud (tipped his son about Innate Immunotherapeutics' failed drug trial) and false statements to the FBI (18 U.S.C. 1001)
Outcome: Pleaded guilty Oct 2019; sentenced Jan 17, 2020, to 26 months and a $200,000 fine; pardoned Dec 22, 2020
Primary source: justice.gov; DOJ pardon list: justice.gov
trading-29.label: Verified by SwampForce

trading-30.title: Former Rep. Stephen Buyer (R-IN)
lines: Charge / court: S.D.N.Y. No. 22-cr-397. Four counts of securities fraud (Sprint/T-Mobile and Navigant/Guidehouse). Charged after he left Congress, for trades as a consultant
Outcome: Jury conviction March 2023; sentenced to 22 months, $354,027.72 forfeiture, and a $10,000 fine; pardoned June 2026
Primary source: Gov't sentencing submission: storage.courtlistener.com; DOJ: justice.gov; pardon: whitehouse.gov
trading-30.label: Verified by SwampForce

trading-31.title: Fed Chair Jerome Powell and former Vice Chair Richard Clarida
lines: Finding: Fed OIG (July 2022; full report Jan 2024) found their trading did not violate applicable laws, rules, or policies. Clarida omitted some trades from disclosures, and a Powell family-trust adviser traded during an FOMC blackout without Powell's knowledge
trading-31.label: Verified by SwampForce

trading-32.title: Former Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan and former Boston Fed President Eric Rosengren
lines: Finding: Fed OIG (2024) found no violation of laws or trading rules, but said their activity created appearance problems (Kaplan's incomplete disclosures; Rosengren's unreported trades)
trading-32.label: Verified by SwampForce
